description: F (Fisher-Snedecor) distribution quantile function F^-1(p; d1, d2)

tolerance.reason: d1, d2 and p are exact doubles and 1 - p is exact for p >= 1/2, but in the tails the quantile is x = exp(L) with L of the order of log(p) / a (lower tail) or -log(1 - p) / b (upper tail); rounding L (or 1/a, 1/b, d2/d1, which multiply it) to a double changes x by |L| times 2^-53. The largest |L| at a positive, normal quantile on this grid is 690.8 (d1 = 2, p = 1e-300, x = 1e-300), so up to 7.7e-14 is unavoidable; 2e-13 allows 2.6x that and matches betaincinv. SciPy's worst error at the points it gets within tolerance is 1.8e-13 (d1 = d2 = 1000, p = 1e-100); it fails 101 points, all with p <= 1e-100: NaN at 27 points, numbers from 1.1e-308 to 4.5e-303 where the quantile is 0 or subnormal (41 points), and errors from 8.5e-12 to 911x at 33 points (e.g. 3e-5 instead of 6.7e-4 at d1 = 1e5, d2 = 1, p = 5e-324)

grid: d1, d2 in {0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 100, 1000, 1e5} (every pair) x p in {0, 5e-324, 1e-300, 1e-100, 1e-20, 1e-10, 1e-5, 1e-3, 0.01, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999, and the doubles nearest 1 - 1e-5, 1 - 1e-10, 1 - 1e-15, 1}; the quantile is 0 at p = 0 (the end of the support) and p = 1 is tagged pole (+inf); quantiles beyond the largest double are tagged overflow
